the virulent strain was able to multiply in the lung and the avirulent strain was unable to do so.
the virulent strain of LP multiplies in the lungs of guinea-pig, is predominantly intracellular and is not destroyed in the lungs by the PMNL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
virulence of L. pneumophila in guinea-pigs is dependent on the ability of the organism to replicate intracellularly.
the virulent strain is more resistant to the killing mechanisms of the macrophages.
the avirulent LP is rapidly cleared from the lungs by the phagocytic cells and the virulent strain is able to multiply in the lung and disseminate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the virulence of L. pneumophila strains can be assessed in the guinea-pig model.
there are differences in virulence between strains of Legionella, and these are reflected in the way the bacteria interact with the host cells.
the macrophages are the major host cell in the lung for Legionella pneumophia.
